_doc: Fact registry for on-screen text validation. Each entry: the claim as we teach it, and machine rules. 'forbid' patterns fail on-screen text. 'hedge' requires one of the hedge words in the same text. Ported from apush-episode-kit, adapted to our review findings.

facts.claim: Disease mortality in the Americas was 50-90% overall, with the hardest-hit towns reaching 90%. Do not present '8-9 out of 10 died' as a universal figure.

forbid.why: drops the script's hedge ('in the hardest-hit towns,' 50-90% overall)
drops the script's hedge ('in the hardest-hit towns,' 50-90% overall)

sources: Review 2026-10-07: script hedges as 'in the hardest-hit towns, 50-90% overall'

facts.claim: Europe gained calories (maize, potatoes) and wealth; the Americas gained wheat, sugar, horses but paid with massive population loss. Do not write that Europe 'won' and stop.

forbid.why: box-3 exam trap: the Americas got wheat, sugar, and the horse — don't write that Europe 'won' and stop
box-3 exam trap: evaluate both halves, don't declare a winner

sources: Review 2026-10-07: box-3 exam trap says not to write that Europe 'won'

facts.claim: Syphilis may have crossed from the Americas to Europe; the origin is debated. Do not present disease as one-way-only.

forbid.why: overclaims against the hedged syphilis beat (Columbian vs pre-Columbian hypotheses debated)
overclaims against the hedged syphilis beat

sources: Review 2026-10-07: caption 'DISEASE: One way only' overclaims against hedged syphilis beat

facts.claim: The Florentine Codex was compiled decades after the conquest under Franciscan oversight. It is not a contemporary eyewitness account.

forbid.why: the card presents a paraphrase as an excerpt — label it 'Paraphrased from the Florentine Codex'

sources: Review 2026-10-07: Codex compiled decades later under Franciscan oversight, say so explicitly

facts.claim: Tomatoes reached Europe after 1492 but were not immediately adopted. Do not imply they arrived in 1492.

forbid.why: implies tomatoes arrived in 1492 — use 'UNTIL AFTER 1492'

sources: Review 2026-10-07: 'NO TOMATOES IN ROME BEFORE 1492' implies arrival in 1492
